question: A 22-year-old Caucasian female presents with severe right lower quadrant pain, malaise, and diarrhea. The physician performs an endoscopy and finds disease involvement in the terminal ileum, noting that that the disease process is patchy with normal intervening mucosa. The entire wall of the region is thickened and inflamed, which may directly lead to formation of:?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Thickened and inflamed wall in terminal ileum" -> "Formation of fistulas" -> 80% CHAIN: "Thickened and inflamed wall in terminal ileum" -> "Widening of the intestinal lumen" -> 70% CHAIN: "Thickened and inflamed wall in terminal ileum" -> "Paneth cell metaplasia" -> 60% CHAIN: "Thickened and inflamed wall in terminal ileum" -> "Formation of fistulas" -> "Toxic megacolon" -> 80%
analysis: The presentation of severe right lower quadrant pain, diarrhea, and disease involvement in the terminal ileum with patchy inflammation and thickening of the wall is indicative of Crohn's disease. The thickened and inflamed wall can lead to the formation of fistulas.
